response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT o.timespan AS timespan, AVG(f.rebrate * 1.0 / f.feerate) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), a AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, SUM(g.cnt) AS total_fee_records, AVG(g.cnt - a.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_mean_count FROM g CROSS JOIN a WHERE g.cnt > a.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: Each group's fee-record count is the number of joined fee rows (COUNT(*)), which equals the number of fees with a matching order since recordvault is treated as unique per order.

The ratio rebrate/feerate is computed per fee row. In SQLite a zero feerate gives NULL on division, so those rows are ignored in the average, the same as rows with a missing rebrate or feerate. They still count toward the fee-record count.
Orders with a NULL timespan, if any, form their own group and count toward the cross-group average like any other group.
